newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mixed before data, pork bellies slip.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mixed before data, pork bellies slip.

text.p: CME hog futures remained mixed at the close on position squaring ahead of the quarterly USDA Hogs and Pigs report while pork bellies ended mostly lower.

Hog futures closed 0.400 cent per lb higher to 0.350 lower with April off 0.325 at 72.475 cents. August finished up most after posting a new contract high of 77.100 cents. Pork bellies ended 1.000 lower to 0.225 higher with only February up and May off 0.825 at 75.125 cents.
Rolling of long April contracts into June by funds weighed on April while positioning ahead of the report and the Taiwan pork ban influenced other months, traders said.

Funds moved out of long April contracts ahead of that month shifting to the spot position after the weekend. However, most of the activity came from position squaring ahead of the hog report to be released at 1400 CST, they said.

Analysts' estimates for all U.S. hogs averaged 99.2 percent of a year ago in a range of 97 to 100.9 percent. Hogs kept for breeding estimates averaged 101.4 percent of a year ago and ranged 98.5 to 104 and hogs kept for market averaged 99 percent and ranged 96 to 100.8 percent.

The Taiwan pork ban again provided underlying strength to summer months. Expectations are that demand for U.S. pork will be at its highest during the third quarter due to the ban, as Taiwan's pork export customers by then will have likely depleted stored pork stocks, analysts said.
The latest CME lean hog index jumped $2.10 to $69.80 per cwt. The gains reflected the surge in cash hog prices after Taiwan's ban on pork exports was announced last week.

Slow trade ahead of the report and lower cash pork belly prices weighed on pork bellies, traders said. Domestic demand again abated when cash bellies rose to the $75-per-cwt level early this week and cash prices have been slipping since, traders said.
USDA reported 14- to 16-lb bellies at midday were down another $1 to $2 at $68.50 to $71.00 per cwt.

E.D.&F. Man notably spread long June hogs/short April while locals covered shorts on the scale down. Rosenthal Collins and ABN Chicogo Corp notably bought August. In hog futures, volatility was up with commission houses buying puts and calls to position ahead of the report, pit sources said.
Rand Financials was a notable buyer of May bellies while ING, E.D.&F. Man and Smith Barney sold, pit sources added.
